paper.title: JARVIS-Leaderboard: a large scale benchmark of materials design methods
paper.research_summary: This work introduces JARVIS-Leaderboard, an open-source and community-driven platform that facilitates benchmarking and enhances reproducibility for materials design methods across multiple categories: Artificial Intelligence (AI), Electronic Structure (ES), Force-fields (FF), Quantum Computation (QC), and Experiments (EXP). It enables users to set up benchmarks with custom tasks and contributions in the form of dataset, code, and metadata submissions, covering various data modalities including atomic structures, spectra, images, and text. The platform includes 1281 contributions to 274 benchmarks using 152 methods with more than 8 million data points.

task.objective: to provide a comprehensive framework for systematic, reproducible, transparent, and unbiased scientific development through large-scale benchmarking of materials design methods
constraints: benchmarks must have digital object identifier (DOI) from peer-reviewed article
contributions must include run script, metadata file, and be reproducible
experimental data used as reference where available
high-fidelity computational methods used as reference when experimental data unavailable
input_requirements: well-characterized/well-known samples/tasks with DOI/peer-reviewed article links
scripts/metadata easily available to reproduce results
contributions in csv.zip format with matching test identifiers
output_goal: leaderboard rankings by performance metric (e.g., MAE)
comparative analysis across methods and categories
interactive plots and tools for method comparison
identification of material space requiring high-fidelity methods
error estimation and validation of electronic structure methods

evidence.text: This work introduces JARVIS-Leaderboard, an open-source and community-driven platform that facilitates benchmarking and enhances reproducibility.
The goal of this project is to provide a more comprehensive framework for materials benchmarking than previous works.

stages.stage_goal: to generate well-defined benchmark datasets with reference data from experimental, density functional theory, or numerical solutions published in peer-reviewed articles

evidence.text: There are several categories for the benchmarks, including AI, ES, QC, FF, and EXP and their combinations.
A benchmark should be considered the “ground truth” for a particular task. Therefore, it is mandatory to have a digital object identifier (DOI) for each benchmark from a peer-reviewed article.

stages.stage_name_raw: generating benchmark datasets with defined data splits
stages.stage_goal: to prepare benchmark datasets with well-defined train/validation/test splits for AI methods and reference test sets for other methods
stage_output: json.zip files with training/validation/test identifiers and target data for AI
reference test sets for ES, FF, QC, EXP

evidence.text: AI benchmarks have pre-defined training/validation/test identifiers and target data in a corresponding json.zip file, while other methods have only reference test set for evaluation because they do not require model training like an AI method does.

stages.stage_name_raw: user submission of methods and models
stages.stage_goal: to enable users to apply their methods, train models, or run experiments on benchmark datasets

evidence.text: A user can apply their method, train models, or run experiments on that dataset and prepare a csv.zip file, a metadata.json file, and also if possible, a conda environment.yaml/Nix/Dockerfile and a run.sh file.

stages.stage_name_raw: computing performance metrics against reference benchmarks
stages.stage_goal: to calculate performance metrics (e.g., MAE, accuracy) for contributions against reference benchmark data

evidence.text: We use several metrics in the leaderboard depending on the “sub-categories” mentioned above. We use mean absolute error (MAE), accuracy (acc), multi-mae (L1 norm of multi-dimensional data), recall-oriented understudy for gisting evaluation (ROUGE) for the single property prediction, single property classification, spectra/eigensolver/atomic forces and textGen/text summary subcategories respectively.

stages.stage_name_raw: reproducing contributions via automated scripts and infrastructure
stages.stage_goal: to verify reproducibility of contributions using run scripts, Dockerfiles, and GitHub actions

evidence.text: This step helps to reproduce the benchmark. These files are kept in a folder with the name of the folder as the team name and can be uploaded to a user’s GitHub account by the automated jarvis_upload.py script.
The contribution addition and automated testings are carried out using GitHub actions.

stages.stage_goal: to establish experimental benchmarks through inter-laboratory testing of the same material/property

evidence.text: Benchmarking experiments essentially boils down to the comparison of different experiments for the same desired result/s. A systematic way to perform this benchmarking is through round-robin testing.
Specifically in the JARVIS-Leaderboard, we include experimental round-robin results for manometric measurements of CO2 adsorption.
